- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven resilience.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility; for 30-day forecasts, apply 10–15% smoothing to avoid overfitting to recent noise.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.80, 0.27, 0.80), model tends to misalign with mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 10–15-day moving average of history.
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome by >10% for 3 consecutive days, reduce forecast by 5–10% and check sentiment for confirmation of bearish shift.
